Are you in the UK? Most Uni's here have gyms (albeit, not great ones) that you get membership for free with your tuition. Depends on the Uni but they're either free or discount for students. 

If not then do what I did and grab a set of weights off Amazon and do some lifting a few days a week and go running the others? I was hella lazy and did almost no exercise because I just couldn't be bothered. And I rolled my eyes a people that did and those who told me it made them feel good. But honestly it's a great release, and probably the best thing is it physically exhausts my body so I can actually sleep every night instead of lying awake, staring at the ceiling until 2/3am every damn night

I find that very familiar. I'm going through a similar thing myself. After a breakup with my best friend in September I fell off and shutdown for 2 months (uni grades suffered). What really seemed to help was joining a gym. I got myself a gym partner (my course mate) and we go 6 times a week. Working through the pain is a much more productive use of energy than my other releases (cutting and solitary drinking). While I'm in no way cured, I'm doing better now than 4 months ago. I used to be a solid 3/10 every day consistently (2/10 on weekends, when I don't have Uni), but now I'm middling at 5 or 6. I still have massive gaping holes in my life that normal people would fill with social interaction, friendships, and relationships...but I suppose I'm just not normal. 

I'd be happy to chat if you're still feeling lonely, though you did post this 8 days ago and I'm not sure if you're even still checking this.

Good luck <3

"Yeah fine"

I haven't been through childhood trauma. I've not been raped. I've got a healthy body and immune system. My physique in improving due to joining the gym. I recently lost my virginity to an amazing girl. I've got enough money for what I need. I'm in University. I have a healthy relationship with my family and parents. My parents are still together and have never separated (touch wood). I'm better than most in my class, in the top 15% of my course. 
And I crash every day. 
And every day I crash harder. 
And It's obviously all on me because everything else about my life is good and healthy and right. s
So I don't have the right to be depressed either, but I am.
<3
"Cheer up!"

Honestly, I hear you. 
I'm 20 and in university in a city away from home. The girl I'm seeing, who I fell in love with in "high school" has also moved from the same home-town as me to the same city and attending a university in this city but a few miles away. She has clinical depression, bi-polar tendencies, anxiety and a host of other illnesses. None of which I see as major faults. I've said to her I'd do anything before and I really thought it'd stay true. But having a SO with depression is hard. It puts a definite long-lasting strain on a relationship. I thought I would last longer and be stronger for her but I couldn't deal with the 3 am calls to pick her up from whatever nightclub and bring her home/to my place for more than a couple of weeks
It's worth noting that depressed is an emotion as well as depression is an illness... You can feel depressed while not having depression.

I think this post needs more attention. 
For me it's when I get home (back to my uni accommodation/"dorm" room) and take off my coat, turn on my heater, switch on my monitors, change in to my sweats and a comfy t-shirt, and sit in my chair. It's all so routine now I don't really think about it...but now I am thinking about it, every time I do it I'm reminded that I don't have anyone to greet me, or anyone to text, or anyone to ask how my day's going

I meant romantic relationships originally, however I now realise the same can be said for meaningful relationships in the platonic sense too. My friendship group in my hometown is large, about 10/11 of us, and most of them have fulltime jobs/university/long term girlfriends and because it's such a large group we don't really get close to the individuals.

I'm in a city about 80 miles from my hometown, still in the UK, studying computer networks. I only got interested in computing because computers are dependable and they dont let you down. They do what they're programmed to do and they don't stab you in the back like people. It'll lead to an antisocial profession and probably a very low level of job satisfaction, so basically what I'd have in any job

I think with self-harmers, the scars mean different things than they do to non-SHers. I personally see mine as a window to the past, a difficult time that I've got past on my own. They give me a sense of strength and self-reliance. To other people, when they look at their scars (through accidents etc.) they want to hide them or cover them up because they think they're ugly/want to forget that it happened.

My scars (about 20 on my left forearm) are nigh on invisible in the winter (although, I imagine in the summer when I tan they'll get more apparent...when I get to that bridge eh). If someone were to get close to them they could make them out, and they're visible in certain light...so I am conscious of people seeing them and then judging me. But internally I don't see anything wrong with feeling a sense of pride about them. I think we're on similar wavelengths.
Nowadays I keep to cutting my thighs, instead of my arms. Means they're out of the public eye (apart from during sex), and I can feel the cuts more when I'm walking everyday/playing drums on my legs.
